title: Human Correction Lesson
description: A structured, before/after shape for a memory.py kind="debug_lesson" record that captures a real human's correction of a real agent mistake -- section 227 of the Research_Capability_Evolution master prompt. Distinct from a self-derived debug_lesson (engine._promote_experience_knowledge()'s own free-text 'captures what this class of problem looks like' kind): this schema requires BOTH sides of the correction (what the agent wrongly believed/did, and what the human corrected it to, with the human's own cited evidence and identity) plus a stable, exact-match mistake_signature_key so a future session can query whether this exact mistake has already been corrected once, instead of re-deriving the same wrong answer and needing a second human correction. Matching is deliberately EXACT (a sha256 of normalized mistake_category + before.claim text), never fuzzy -- the same discipline this project's other exact-equality signature keys (evidence_db.signature_key(), user_correction_trigger.correction_signature_key()) already apply, for the identical reason: a fuzzy join would silently group two unrelated mistakes as "the same one", manufacturing a false sense that a mistake class was already handled.

kind.description: The existing memory.py/memory_router.py kind this record is a structured extension of -- never a new sixth kind.

mistake_category.description: What class of mistake this is (e.g. hallucinated_vip_api, wrong_bind_location, fabricated_evidence, misidentified_root_cause). Free text, but never empty -- a correction record with no stated mistake class has nothing for query_prior_correction() to group future occurrences of the same mistake against.

mistake_signature_key.description: sha256 of {mistake_category, before.claim}, both whitespace/case-normalized -- the exact-match key find_prior_corrections()/has_prior_correction() query against. Computed by mistake_signature_key(), never hand-typed by a caller.

lesson.description: The reusable, human-readable claim this record carries for memory_router.engineering_admission_gate()'s REUSABLE check (root_cause/fix/lesson) -- synthesized from before/after, never left blank.

evidence.description: Top-level mirror of correction.after.evidence, satisfying engineering_admission_gate()'s EVIDENCE check -- the same field every other engineering-tier record is admitted on.

confidence.description: memory_router.ENGINEERING_ADMISSION_CONFIDENCE_LEVELS -- a real human's direct correction is, by this project's own existing confidence vocabulary, at minimum HIGH.

verified.description: A human correction that actually happened is, by definition, verified -- never a caller-settable false claim about an unconfirmed mistake.

reusable.description: A captured lesson is explicitly reusable by future sessions -- the whole point of this record.

correction_source.description: Distinguishes this record from a self-derived debug_lesson (engine._promote_experience_knowledge()'s own kind); never inferred, always the literal fact of who produced the 'after' side.

claim.description: What the agent wrongly asserted or did -- the mistake itself, in the agent's own words/action, never paraphrased by the human's correction.

reasoning.description: Why the agent believed the mistaken claim, when known -- optional context, never required (an agent's own reasoning is not always recoverable after the fact).

claim.description: The corrected fact/action, as the human stated it.

evidence.description: The human's own cited basis for the correction (e.g. an RTL file:line, a VIP manual section, a spec citation) -- an uncited correction is an opinion, not evidence, and this project's Evidence Truth Rule forbids treating the two alike.

corrected_by.description: Who made the correction -- never anonymous; a correction attributed to nobody cannot be distinguished from the agent correcting itself.
